cards.title: 'Review after 1 month' is not optional
cards.body: Those words at the bottom of the prescription get ignored a lot. They are the doctor's plan to check whether the treatment is working.

cards.title: It's a check-in, not a repeat
cards.body: The doctor wants to see how the body responded. The medicine, the dose or the tests may change based on what they find.

cards.title: It's not a refill instruction
cards.body: Buying the same strips again at the chemist is not a review. Ask your doctor before continuing a course past the review date.

cards.title: Something usually needs checking
cards.body: Often the doctor wants readings, a blood test or a look at side effects. Ask during the visit what the review is for, so you come prepared.

cards.title: Put the date in the calendar today
cards.body: Count a month from the visit and set a reminder a few days early. Book the slot before the medicine runs out, not after.

cards.title: Going earlier is fine if things change
cards.body: If symptoms get worse or new side effects show up, call the doctor sooner. Chest pain, fainting or sudden weakness mean 112 right away.

takeaway: 'Review after 1 month' means the doctor wants to check the treatment, so book it early and bring what they asked for.
share: 'Review after 1 month' on the prescription is part of the treatment. Put it in the calendar.
